ga_power_marginal_per_kwh.notes: Dollars per kWh. Schedule R-31 (bills from June 2026). Block: the 651 to 1000 kWh block in summer (Next 350 kWh, 14.5738¢), the only block in winter (All kWh, 8.2116¢); team decision, not a claim about typical household usage. Season weighting from the tariff's billing months: 4 summer (June to September), 8 winter (October to May). Base = (4 x 14.5738 + 8 x 8.2116) / 12 = 10.332333¢. Riders applied per kWh: ECCR-15 13.0205% and DSM-R-16 1.1969% of the base bill (source ids ga_power_eccr, ga_power_dsm_r), adding 10.332333 x 0.142174 = 1.468989¢; FCR-27 fuel for secondary distribution customers (ga_power_fcr), (4 x 3.8069 + 8 x 3.8561) / 12 = 3.839700¢. Total = 15.641022¢ = $0.15641. ECCR and DSM-R are included because both apply to every residential bill as a percentage of the base bill, so each added kWh raises them in proportion; without them the rate would be 10.332333 + 3.839700 = 14.172033¢ ($0.14172). Left out: basic service charge ($0.4603 per day, fixed, not per kWh) and MFF-11 municipal franchise fee (ga_power_mff; 3.0843% inside or 1.1995% outside city limits, depends on location).

egrid_ga_kg_per_kwh.notes: Kilograms CO2e per kWh. eGRID2023 rev2 Table 1, subregion SRSO (SERC South), total output emission rate, CO2e 846.007 lb/MWh x 0.45359237 kg/lb / 1000 kWh/MWh = 0.383742. Total output chosen (team decision) because the carbon line is the footprint of the electricity the unit consumes, which is what eGRID's total output rates describe. For reference, the SRSO non-baseload CO2e rate is 1392.345 lb/MWh = 0.631557 kg/kWh (not used).

g19_card_apr_assessed.notes: Annual rate as a fraction. Federal Reserve G.19 released September 8, 2026, Terms of Credit, commercial bank interest rates on credit card plans, accounts assessed interest, 2026 Q2: 22.15 percent (not seasonally adjusted). Latest quarter published in that release.

pal_rate_cap.notes: Annual rate as a fraction. 12 CFR 701.21(c)(7)(iv)(A): PALs II may charge '1000 basis points above the maximum interest rate established by the Board'. The Board's ceiling is 18 percent through September 10, 2027 (source id ncua_rate_ceiling, press release of February 6, 2026). 18% + 10% = 28%. A ceiling, never a rate a user can get.

pal_fee_cap.notes: Dollars. 12 CFR 701.21(c)(7)(iv)(A)(6): 'a reasonable application fee ... but that in no case exceeds $20'.

pal_max_amount.notes: Dollars. 12 CFR 701.21(c)(7)(iv)(A)(1): 'The principal of the payday alternative loan is not more than $2,000'. Maturity per (A)(2): one to 12 months.
